SourcesBox score, game stories and the drawn play

Box score from the 76ers' 123–112 win over the Toronto Raptors at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Nov 12, 2026, from the Bleacher Report box score (points, rebounds, assists, blocks and steals) and the FOX Sports line score and key lines, with game details from the Associated Press (via WRAL), Field Level Media (via KMJ and Yardbarker), NBC Sports Philadelphia, Philly Sports Reports, Metro Philadelphia and Yahoo Sports. All 123 Philadelphia points are accounted for by eight players in the box score. Barrett's 31 points (13 of 20) and 14 rebounds and Quickley's 26 points are from Bleacher Report, FOX Sports, Field Level Media and NBC Sports (the AP's early story had Quickley at 25); the lines found this morning account for 99 of Toronto's 112 points, and none of the other Raptors appear in this recap. The quarter scores add up to both totals (60–60 at the half, matching NBC Sports Philadelphia and Philly Sports Reports; 96–87 after three, matching the AP). Toronto's 17-point lead was 33–16 late in the first quarter: Field Level Media, Metro Philadelphia and Philly Sports Reports have 17, and the 8–0 run that ended the quarter at 33–24 starts from 33–16 (the AP has 16). Maxey's 8 of 13 is from FOX Sports, Brown's 8 of 15 and Embiid's 6 of 7 at the line from Yahoo Sports, Simons' 5 of 6 from three from NBC Sports Philadelphia. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Thursday's games: Philadelphia 10–3 and second in the East, Indiana 4–8.

LeBron James missed his third straight game with a back injury (AP). Toronto was without Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes (AP, Field Level Media). Embiid left briefly after a knee-to-knee collision in the first quarter and returned (AP, NBC Sports Philadelphia). Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker went 9 of 13 from three off the bench (Bleacher Report); Edgecombe's 8 assists were a season high (NBC Sports Philadelphia). Toronto had seven turnovers in the third quarter (Field Level Media). Philadelphia hosts Indiana on Sunday at 1:00 PM ET (Field Level Media, Metro Philadelphia).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Anfernee Simons' 3-pointer at the first-quarter buzzer, which cut Toronto's lead from 33–21 to 33–24 and capped an 8–0 Philadelphia run to end the quarter (NBC Sports Philadelphia, Philly Sports Reports, Metro Philadelphia). Philly Sports Reports describes Simons as wide open; the move isn't described further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Simons' listed 6-foot-4 and 200 pounds (Wikipedia), with arms scaled to the 6-foot-9¼ wingspan measured at the 2018 draft combine (NBC Sports), in Philadelphia's home white with No. 5 (Wikipedia, RealGM). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with our default skin tone. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
